facts.raw_span: A 36-year-old man with no prior medical history presented with a 4-year history of diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows and intermittent generalized pruritus
his bone pain worsened and he developed blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
White-cell count and differential: normal
Hemoglobin: normal
Platelet count: mild thrombocytosis (120 × 10^9/L)
C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: mildly elevated
Knee radiographs: bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes of the distal femora and proximal tibiae
99mTc bone scintigraphy and FDG-PET: bilateral symmetric uptake in long bones, right clavicle, and mandible, with uptake in subcutaneous and muscle tissues of the lower limbs
CT-guided biopsy of the left proximal tibia showed diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells
Immunohistochemical staining of the histiocytes was positive for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa, and negative for CD1a, S100, and langerin
MRI of the brain: enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues
PET/CT of the brain: corresponding FDG-avid lesions

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain, sclerotic changes on radiographs, and diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes on biopsy is consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease, a rare multisystem disorder.

The patient's thrombocytosis, elevated inflammatory markers, and enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues are suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, a hematologic and lymphatic disorder.
The patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain, sclerotic changes on radiographs, and bilateral symmetric uptake on bone scintigraphy is also consistent with sarcoidosis, a multisystem disorder.
The patient's sclerotic changes on radiographs and bilateral symmetric uptake on bone scintigraphy could also be consistent with bone metastasis, a bone and joint disease.
The patient's thrombocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers could also be suggestive of multiple myeloma, a hematologic and lymphatic disorder.
The patient's sclerotic changes on radiographs and bilateral symmetric uptake on bone scintigraphy could also be consistent with Paget's disease of bone, a bone and joint disease.
The patient's sclerotic changes on radiographs and bilateral symmetric uptake on bone scintigraphy could also be consistent with osteopetrosis, a bone and joint disease.
The patient's diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes on biopsy is consistent with histiocytosis, a multisystem disorder.
